/study/macbeth/.title: Macbeth
/study/macbeth/.author: William Shakespeare
description: The Astor Study Edition of Macbeth is written for students at school and university. It contains the full text of the play, with line numbers, a summary of every scene, explanatory notes, context, key quotations and analysis written for GCSE and A-level.
It gives particular attention to ambition, responsibility, equivocation, gender, imagery, character and performance.
contents: The full text of the play, with line numbers
Analysis written for GCSE and A-level
/study/macbeth/.summary: What the witches actually promise, the murder and the sleeplessness after it, and the images of blood, sleep and darkness that come back throughout the play.

description: The Astor Study Edition of Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde is written for students at school and university. It contains the complete text, chapter summaries, explanatory notes, context, key quotations and help with essays.
It gives particular attention to duality, secrecy, science, setting and the way the story is told.
list.summary: Utterson’s investigation chapter by chapter, the science Jekyll claims, and the confession that explains the door in the back street.

list.title: Frankenstein
list.author: Mary Shelley
description: The Astor Study Edition of Frankenstein is written for students at school and university. It contains the full, unabridged text, chapter summaries, key quotations, context and literary analysis.
It gives particular attention to creation, responsibility, isolation, the frame narrative, science and sympathy.
list.summary: Three narrators inside one another, the creature’s self-education, the companion he demands, and the pursuit into the ice.

list.title: Dracula
list.author: Bram Stoker
description: The Astor Study Edition of Dracula is written for students at school and university. It contains The 1897 text, a companion to each chapter, key quotations, characters, context and critical perspectives.
list.summary: The journals, letters and telegrams the novel is assembled from, the hunt from Whitby to Transylvania, and what the men decide for Mina.

list.title: Great Expectations
list.author: Charles Dickens
description: The Astor Study Edition of Great Expectations is written for students at school and university. It contains the full text, chapter summaries, context and key quotations for exams.
list.summary: Pip’s three stages, the money and where it really came from, Miss Havisham, Magwitch, and both of Dickens’s endings.

list.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
list.author: Oscar Wilde
description: The Astor Study Edition of The Picture of Dorian Gray is written for students at school and university. It contains the complete novel, commentary and analysis, what critics have argued, analysis of key quotations and context.
list.summary: The portrait, the wish Dorian makes in Chapter 2, Lord Henry’s influence, and the epigrams that carry the argument.

list.title: Tess of the d’Urbervilles
list.author: Thomas Hardy
description: The Astor Study Edition of Tess of the d’Urbervilles is written for students at school and university. It contains the complete novel, support for each chapter, analysis of key quotations, criticism and model paragraphs.
list.summary: Tess’s work and wages, the night at Trantridge, the two confessions, and the judgement Hardy puts in his subtitle.

list.title: Moby-Dick
list.author: Herman Melville
description: The Astor Study Edition of Moby-Dick is written for students at school and university. It contains analysis of each chapter, context, themes and what critics have argued.
list.summary: Ahab’s quarrel, Ishmael’s voice, the whaling trade that pays for the voyage, and the chapters that stop being a novel.

list.title: Mrs Dalloway
list.author: Virginia Woolf
description: The Astor Study Edition of Mrs Dalloway is written for students at school and university. It contains annotations, analysis, themes, context, characters and critical perspectives.
list.summary: One day in June, a party being prepared, Septimus and his doctors, and the moment the two stories touch.

list.title: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
list.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
description: The Astor Study Edition of The Rime of the Ancient Mariner is written for students at school and university. It contains the complete poem, commentary, context, key quotations, themes and what critics have argued.
It gives particular attention to the seven parts, language, imagery and essay writing.
list.summary: The voyage, the bird, a punishment out of all proportion, and the marginal gloss Coleridge added twenty years later.

list.title: Macbeth and Jekyll and Hyde
list.author: Two texts in one volume
description: This Study Edition prints two texts often studied together, with study material for each.
list.summary: Ambition, guilt, duality, secrecy, violence, the supernatural and moral collapse.

list.title: Macbeth and A Christmas Carol
list.author: Two texts in one volume
description: This Study Edition prints two texts often studied together, with study material for each.
list.summary: Power, guilt, supernatural warning, social responsibility and transformation.

list.title: Romeo and Juliet and Jekyll and Hyde
list.author: Two texts in one volume
description: This Study Edition prints two texts often studied together, with study material for each.
list.summary: Conflict, identity, secrecy, violence and destructive choices.

list.title: Romeo and Juliet and A Christmas Carol
list.author: Two texts in one volume
description: This Study Edition prints two texts often studied together, with study material for each.
list.summary: Family, social pressure, change, responsibility and moral consequence.
